title: urn:qauth:ia:captcha:v1-rc.0
description: A bot challenge, when a soft threshold requires one; the pending step resumes after it (ADR-017 Decisions 4 and 7). By default the built-in proof of work, whose script the ceremony app serves from the realm origin. An operator may name a hosted provider for the sign-up and sign-in pages only (ADR-019 Decision 5). A required challenge needs JavaScript and is never skipped. The built-in proof of work (`provider` `pow`) is solved as follows. The answer, `captcha_token`, is a nonce: 1 to 16 ASCII digits `0` to `9`, with no sign and no leading zero (`0` itself is a nonce). The engine takes the SHA-256 digest of the UTF-8 bytes of the challenge, a colon and the nonce, `<challenge>:<nonce>`, with the challenge as the text it is, not base64url-decoded. It accepts the nonce when that digest starts with at least `difficulty` zero bits, read from the most significant bit of its first byte. Any such nonce passes; trying 0, 1, 2 and so on finds one after about 2^`difficulty` hashes. A puzzle takes one answer: a wrong one gets the step back with `captcha_failed` and a new challenge. QAuth’s shared test vectors, `test-vectors/interaction/proof-of-work.json` in its repository, hold cases to check a solver against.

params.description: The challenge to solve: the built-in proof of work, or a hosted provider.

challenge.description: The puzzle the engine issued, hashed as the text it is.

difficulty.description: The fewest leading zero bits the SHA-256 digest of `<challenge>:<nonce>` must start with.

provider.description: A hosted provider the operator named.

name.description: The name the operator gave the hosted provider.

captcha_token.description: For the built-in proof of work, the nonce: 1 to 16 ASCII digits, with no sign and no leading zero. For a hosted provider, the provider’s token. Printable ASCII, so 4096 characters are 4096 bytes.

error.description: Why the last answer was refused. A closed set.

amr.description: The RFC 8176 `amr` values a successful answer adds to the transaction: none, because the step proves no authenticator.
